This was my first hitman game that I played back on my PS4, revisiting on PC was great. There's obviously this circlejerk in the hitman community to hate on this one. I'd ignore all that and just go for it, especially if it's on sale. Probably the most in depth game that lets Agent 47 have some character and not act like a machine the whole time. The voice actor for 47 says this is his favorite game! It's super fun, give it a shot.

Islets is a charming, adorable and fun little metroidvania with smooth, zippy movement, fun gimmicks and real good level design, the music is catchy, bubbly and eerie when it needs to be, definitely excited to see what the Thompson brothers can do next! If its DLC or a sequel, or something entirely new, definitely a team to look forward to from.

The length is perfect, doesn't last too long and isn't too short, just the right amount of length for a metroidvania of this size and one a few others should learn from, definitely worth the £15-£16.

I booted this up expecting a cute little forest romp. Five minutes later, I’m emotionally attached to a child and being hunted by something that looks like a troll crossed with my sleep paralysis demon.

Visually? Gorgeous. Like a Studio Ghibli film fell into a vat of Scandinavian trauma.
Soundtrack? Haunting. Like lullabies sung by a ghost who regrets their life choices.
Gameplay? Mostly me running, hiding, and whispering “no no no nope nope nope” out loud.

The story is surprisingly touching. I left emotionally damaged but in a good way.

Worst part of this game is when it's over. Definitely worth the price tag.
Legitimately a gripping, excellent experience which I hope gets a spiritual successor or a sequel.
Replayability is somewhat good but nowhere near as high as everyone's expectations seem to be going into it.
Atmosphere/ambience is unparalleled, if you actively put effort into getting immersed in the audio you'll be rewarded with an unrivalled experience. 
9/10. Buy the game and support a one of a kind developer.

I've always loved games about selling stuff, tycoon games and games like Recettear so this was right up my alley....never liked underwater games though....but in first person that is, this game has a lovely sidescroller view where underwater enemies doesn't freak me out =p  

Also, for the graphic style I have to say that it's a beautiful game

I wanted to love this game. It's lovely and has a really cool art style. I felt like the premise was strong and it had great potential.

But there are huge design flaws. And it's not bugs; it's the way that the controls were intentionally designed. The wall jump mechanic is super awkward and is a major part of the game, and would be SO much better if it was a normal wall jump that used the jump key to rebound instead of that weird 'left right left right' stuff. And the instant death spikes that are way too prevalent are an annoying obstacle that just drains the pleasure of playing.

The design is cool, and I'd love to go through the story, but these 'innovative things' that the devs came up with should be totally stricken from the game. Do this, and I'll play it.

I don’t usually leave reviews, but this is one time I really want to.

To say this game is a masterpiece would be an understatement. You can feel its soul from the very first second to the very last. It’s a game that will make you laugh, cry, and leave you with a kind of emptiness afterward that very few things can create.

RDR2 is not just a game. It’s a world that makes you fall in love with it and then emotionally destroys you.

It’s a game about beauty and horror.
A game that leaves a mark on you forever.
A unique gaming experience that won’t leave anyone indifferent, where everyone will find something of their own.

It’s a game with a story that isn’t just a “plot”, but something you live through with every cell of your body, alongside the characters.

It’s a game I will definitely remember.

1000000/10

The game seems really fun so far, but the performance is absolutely abysmal. Turning all settings to low doesn't improve anything either.

I've experienced 3 crashes in the first hour of play.

There might be a good game here, but it's buried under technical problems. Really unforgivable when it's asking for precision but doesn't actually give you the tools to meet its requirements. The first boss I was falling through the map, or ended up under them, or even inside them sometimes whenever I dodged. Or I'd get stuck on nothing and just have to wait for them to dispatch me, hoping things might go smoother next time (which they didn't). Sound glitches where it gets stuck on a particularly grating part of the boss encounter and stays that way however many times I reload. Inexplicable performance drops where I have to drop everything down to low, and then it still becomes barely playable at points. I've found myself getting so angry at this game but not for any gameplay reasons. Going to delete it for a while and hope they actually optimise it at some point.

I'd give this a neutral review if I could. The aesthetic and setting are great. Weapons and enemies are decent. Level design is atrocious. A large amount of the game has narrow corridors and square arenas, similar to Wolfenstein 3D. An intermediate Doom mapper could probably make something several times more engaging. I also felt like I was shooting at cardboard cutouts sometimes. The pros barely outweigh the cons for me. Worth trying on a sale.

A unique roguelike where you can practice a fight - to make sure you perfectly choreograph it -- before executing the fight for real. You can practice as many times as you want. If you make a mistake in the real fight and die -- your run ends. 

The game is sufficiently challenging even with the practiced choreography. 

The keyboard controls are also intuitive and simple enough to grasp. This roguelike reminds you an awful lot of Shogun Showdown - it's similar to it, except it has a more real-time tactical element to it rather than being turn based. 

So if you are a fan of Shogun Showdown or Slay the Spire like roguelikes or if you are a fan of real-time tactical games like Desperados 3 or Shadow Tactics, do check this game out.

I was craving a new metroidvania to play and so far Gigasword has scratched that itch. The intro is pretty long, between cutscenes, dialogue, and just the time it takes to really get to interesting enemies and puzzles. Some of the cutscene illustrations of the main hero are funny looking, but that's a minor note. Now that I'm in the castle more I enjoy it a lot. There are smart puzzles utilizing the sword. The combat feels nice with weight behind the sword.

It's February 10th 2012. You just got out of class for the day. You head to Family Video that has an attached Little Ceazers. You go in and grab a brand new copy of The Darkness 2 off the shelf and rent it for a week for $5. You pop into Little Ceazers next door and grab a Hot-N-Ready pepperoni for $5. You go home to your crappy college apartment and play D2 all night and crush that Hot-N-Ready like it was nothing. Didn't really get better than that.
